title: Best Ad Tracking & Targeted Advertising Tools Compared
metaDescription: Compare the top tools to stop ad tracking and prevent targeted advertising. Block behavioral ads, cross-site tracking, and regain your privacy.
intro: Tired of ads following you across the web? This page compares five ways to cut ad tracking: three browser extensions (uBlock Origin, Ghostery and Privacy Badger) and two browsers (DuckDuckGo and Incognito Browser), each scored on the same five criteria.

products.name: uBlock Origin
products.tagline: Open-source ad and tracker blocker with fine-grained filter controls
cons: Requires manual configuration for best results
No longer runs in Chrome, which now only allows the more limited uBlock Origin Lite; the full version works in Firefox, including Firefox for Android

products.name: Incognito Browser
products.tagline: Android browser that stays in private mode and wipes history, cookies and sessions when you exit
pros: Built-in ad blocker, with a High Security Blocking option added in May 2026
Always in private mode: history, cookies and sessions are wiped when you exit the app
Settings to turn images, JavaScript and cookies on or off
cons: Android only: there is no iOS, desktop or web version
No fingerprinting protection and no VPN
Google Play's Data safety section says it may collect crash logs and diagnostics for analytics
Custom filter rules and per-site allowlists are not among its listed features

products.name: Ghostery
products.tagline: Tracker and ad blocker that shows which trackers each site loads
pros: Safari extension on iPhone and iPad; Firefox add-on on Android
cons: Fewer custom filtering options than uBlock Origin

products.name: Privacy Badger
products.tagline: EFF's tracker blocker that stops third parties seen tracking people across sites
pros: Blocks trackers from a list EFF keeps updated by crawling thousands of sites
cons: Blocks only ads that track you, not other ads

products.name: DuckDuckGo Browser
products.tagline: Browser for phone and desktop with automatic tracker blocking
pros: Privacy Dashboard shows the trackers blocked on each site
Privacy policy says it doesn't save your search or browsing history

features.name: Ad Blocking
features.description: Blocks display ads, video ads, and sponsored content

ublock-origin.note: Blocks ads with regularly updated, customizable filter lists

incognito-browser.note: Built-in ad blocker, with a High Security Blocking option since May 2026

ghostery.note: Blocks ads with filter lists, including on YouTube and Facebook (per Ghostery)

privacy-badger.note: Blocks ads that track you, but not other ads: it is a tracker blocker, not an ad blocker

duckduckgo-browser.note: Blocks tracker-based ads and most video ads, including on YouTube (per DuckDuckGo)

features.name: Cross-Site Tracking Prevention
features.description: Stops advertisers from tracking you across different websites

ublock-origin.note: Advanced tracking protection with multiple filter lists

incognito-browser.note: Wipes cookies and sessions on exit and lets you turn cookies off; no tracker blocking within a session is listed

ghostery.note: Blocks trackers from its tracker database

features.name: Fingerprinting Protection
features.description: Prevents websites from identifying you through device characteristics

ublock-origin.note: Blocks known fingerprinting scripts through its filter lists; doesn't change the browser's fingerprint

incognito-browser.note: Not claimed. Agent Cloaking changes the browser and device a site sees, which is not fingerprint protection

ghostery.note: Blocks fingerprinting scripts listed in its tracker database

duckduckgo-browser.note: Blocks fingerprinting scripts and limits the browser APIs they rely on (per DuckDuckGo)

features.name: Ease of Use
features.description: How simple it is to install and configure for optimal protection

ublock-origin.note: Works out of the box; advanced features need setup

incognito-browser.note: Private mode is always on, so there is nothing to set up

ghostery.note: Ad blocking, anti-tracking and Never-Consent are on from install, with no setup needed

privacy-badger.note: Install and forget; works from a tracker list EFF keeps updated

features.name: Customization Options
features.description: Ability to customize blocking rules and whitelist trusted sites

ublock-origin.note: Extensive customization and filter list options

incognito-browser.note: Switches for images, JavaScript, cookies and High Security Blocking; custom rules and per-site allowlists aren't listed

ghostery.note: Good options for trackers and ads, with fewer filter controls than uBlock Origin

privacy-badger.note: Per-site and per-domain controls; few other settings

verdict.summary: Ghostery and uBlock Origin tie for the top score on these five criteria (Ghostery is listed first alphabetically). Ghostery blocks ads and trackers with nothing to set up and shows which trackers each site loads. uBlock Origin gives the most filtering control, though Chrome now only runs the more limited uBlock Origin Lite. DuckDuckGo Browser comes next, with tracker and ad blocking built in on phone and desktop, followed by Privacy Badger, which blocks trackers and the ads that track you but leaves other ads alone. Incognito Browser, which we make, scores lowest: it has a built-in ad blocker and wipes cookies and history when you exit, but it documents no fingerprinting protection or tracker blocking.

bestFor.useCase: Most control over what gets blocked
bestFor.reason: Ties for the top score, with the deepest filter customization (full version on Firefox; Chrome gets uBlock Origin Lite)

bestFor.useCase: Tracker and ad blocking built into the browser
bestFor.reason: Works without setup on Android, iOS, Windows and Mac
Blocks trackers from a list EFF keeps updated, with almost nothing to configure

pro_tips: Use more than one layer: a tracker-blocking browser plus a content-blocking extension catches more than either alone. Check that the extension supports your browser first, since many mobile browsers don't accept extensions.
Regularly clear cookies and browsing data to break existing tracking profiles that advertisers have built about your browsing habits.
Block third-party cookies in your browser settings and turn on Global Privacy Control where your browser offers it; the older 'Do Not Track' signal is widely ignored.
Review and adjust your ad personalization settings on Google, Facebook, and other platforms to limit targeted advertising.
Consider using a VPN alongside tracking protection tools to hide your IP address from advertising networks and data brokers.

faqs.question: Will blocking ad tracking break websites I use regularly?
faqs.answer: Most blockers are built to keep breakage low. uBlock Origin and Ghostery ship filters that fix common problems, and most tools let you pause protection on a single site while keeping it on everywhere else.

faqs.question: How do I know if ad tracking protection is actually working?
faqs.answer: You'll notice fewer targeted ads following you across sites, and tools like Ghostery show what they blocked on each page. You can also test your browser at EFF's Cover Your Tracks (formerly Panopticlick) to see how it handles trackers and fingerprinting.

faqs.question: Can I still support websites while blocking ads and trackers?
faqs.answer: Yes, many ad blockers allow you to whitelist specific sites you want to support. You can also look for direct support options like subscriptions, donations, or merchandise. Some sites offer ad-free experiences for supporters.

faqs.question: What's the difference between blocking ads and blocking tracking?
faqs.answer: Ad blocking removes visible advertisements from web pages, while tracking protection stops companies from collecting data about your browsing habits. Tracking can happen even without visible ads through invisible pixels, analytics scripts, and social media widgets.

faqs.question: Do mobile apps track me the same way websites do?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mobile apps use similar tracking techniques, plus device identifiers and location data. Review app permissions carefully and limit ad tracking in your phone's privacy settings. For browsing, a browser with built-in tracker blocking, such as DuckDuckGo's, limits what websites can track.
